sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet and Sepolia Shadow Fork
sections.summary: Sepolia Shadow Fork launching imminently; CL side has been stable; shadow fork expected to run a day or two before Sepolia upgrade.
sections.body:
- A Sepolia Shadow Fork was being prepared during the call, with launch expected within the hour.
  - Shadow fork expected to remain live for a day or two, shutting down before the weekend.
  - Goal is to verify everything works as expected before the Sepolia fork.
- CL side reported as relatively stable with no issues flagged.
- Potuz requested a small non-finalizing devnet (or reusing devnet-8) to test incident response scenarios such as unfinalized checkpoint syncing.
  - Parithosh agreed to coordinate stopping some nodes on devnet-8 for this purpose, noting resource constraints with multiple devnets already running.

sections.heading: Sepolia Upgrade and Hoodi Timeline
sections.summary: Sepolia forks to Glamsterdam on October 6 at ~13:53 UTC; Hoodi date tentatively the week before Devcon, pending Sepolia outcome.
sections.body:
- Sepolia will fork to Glamsterdam on October 6th at approximately 13:53 UTC.
- Hoodi date has not been formally set yet; proposed for around October 27th (the week before Devcon), contingent on Sepolia going well.
  - Formal Hoodi date decision expected at ACDE next week.
- Barnabas confirmed willingness to schedule Hoodi one week before Devcon.

sections.heading: Incident Response Plan and Coordinator Nominations
sections.summary: Client teams asked to nominate incident response coordinators for Sepolia; Will Corcoran is the communications coordinator.
sections.body:
- The [incident response plan](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/processes/protocol-upgrade.md#incident-response-plan) document was highlighted, encoding postures for handling problems during network upgrades.
- Will Corcoran introduced as communications coordinator; a signal channel was created with EF security, DevOps, and testing teams.
- Parithosh and Barnabas confirmed as DevOps coordinators.
- Justin Traglia and Mario Vega nominated for testing roles (Mario as primary, Justin as backup).
  - Mario noted he can assist with generating test cases on the fly for issues found during the upgrade.
- Client teams asked to nominate their coordinators via PR to the [mainnet plan document](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/glamsterdam-mainnet-plan.md) by end of Monday.
  - Barnabas warned he would pick coordinators for teams that don't self-nominate by Monday.

sections.heading: Hegotá Scoping: Withdrawn EIPs
sections.summary: EIP-8333 (Align Checkpoint with Epoch Boundary Block) and EIP-8363 (Tapered Issuance Burn) both withdrawn from Hegotá consideration.
sections.body:
- EIP-8333 withdrawn by Lodestar/lodekeeper; Cayman explained they looked further at decoupled consensus and decided it's not worth addressing now.
- EIP-8363 withdrawn by its champions; Jerome posted on [ETH Magicians](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8363-tapered-issuance-burn/29263/271) explaining the desire for a broader community-driven process rather than shoehorning a policy change into ACD scoping.
  - A timeline for an alternative approach is included in the post.

sections.heading: EIP-8365 Deposit Guard Update and CFI
sections.summary: EIP-8365 updated to keep only the deposit guard; forced exit split into a standalone future-fork EIP; CFI'd for Hegotá with broad support.
sections.body:
- NC presented the update: the deposit guard portion remains in EIP-8365; the forced exit part has been separated into a standalone EIP not proposed for Hegotá.
- This update was the condition set on the previous call for CFI.
- Agreement: EIP-8365 CFI'd for Hegotá with broad support in chat.
- Barnabas raised whether new 0x01 withdrawal credentials should be disallowed in a future fork.
  - Potuz noted that if EIP-8148 (lowering the compounding threshold) gets in, 0x01 should be disabled in the same fork since there would be no reason not to use 0x02 with a 32 ETH threshold.

sections.heading: Quick Slots (EIP-8198) Discussion and CFI
sections.summary: Quick slots CFI'd for Hegotá after extensive debate; concerns around PQ timeline and testing noted, with understanding it can be pulled before SFI.
sections.body:
- Ryan Berckmans (community guest) spoke in support: L2 and app-layer teams want quick slots included; beginning the system of reducing slot time now reduces risk of 12-second slots persisting for 3-4 more years.
- Barnabé Monnot presented [slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1e8oYeHZ-E4qKplWsL28xt3fpQTNehY_90ENwxh_29N0/edit?usp=sharing) making the case for CFI:
  - Value: better UX, faster confirmation, less MEV leakage, faster finality, more censorship resistance.
  - Specs merged (PR 5592); EIP in review; Prysm prototype implementation ongoing.
  - Ecosystem outreach via Sourcify smart contract analysis underway; ~100 contracts identified as needing review; key teams (Lido, Offchain, EFFI) already confirmed feasibility of adapting.
  - 10 seconds is confident to not block PQ transition given decoupled consensus design (512-validator subcommittee, no aggregation in critical path).
  - Target is 10 seconds for Hegotá (EIP being updated from earlier 8-second figure).
- Lodestar (Nico Flaig) reported having a branch with shorter slots; described as trivial from a code perspective.
- Teku (Enrico Del Fante) rated it S tier; Paul's POC feedback was that it isn't complicated.
- Prysm (Terence) rated it A tier; prototype updated against latest spec; several weeks of detailed audit completed; team considers the trade-off worth it.
- Lighthouse (kingy) did a rough implementation to scope difficulty; mechanically not hard; testing will take time; personally very in favor.
- **Concerns raised:**
  - Lodestar (Matthew Keil / ChainSafe): tuning clients for CPU scheduling under shorter slots is hard; PQ is existential and should have priority; 10 seconds is somewhat arbitrary; work may be wasted when decoupled consensus reworks slot mechanics. However, team is open to adding the machinery to adjust slot times without actually reducing them yet.
  - Grandine (Saulius): not in support; suggested other teams push it and share experience first, similar to stable containers path.
  - Fredrik: concerned about impact on PQ timeline acceleration; supportive of the value but worried about delays to Hegotá.
  - Justin Traglia: initially opposed for Hegotá due to PQ concerns, but softened to supporting CFI after discussion clarified that DC mitigates PQ-related slot time concerns.
  - Lightclient noted it seems contentious and that deciding slot time before implementing the new consensus protocol seems premature.
- **Key counterarguments to PQ concern:**
  - Potuz and Francesco D'Amato: PQ cannot happen without DC anyway; DC removes signature aggregation from the critical path, making slot time largely orthogonal to PQ.
  - Ansgar Dietrichs: if not in Hegotá, likely not in I* (DC too big), J* (PQ focus), so K* in 2029 at earliest.
  - Barnabas: protocol shouldn't be kneecapped today out of fear of future PQ requirements; slot time can always be increased later if needed.
- Łukasz Rozmej (Nethermind): EL tail block processing is 50-200ms P95; CPU not a problem from EL side; zkVMs shouldn't hold protocol hostage; Nethermind pro-CFI.
- Decision: Quick slots (EIP-8198) CFI'd for Hegotá.
  - Understanding: more data needed to validate the 12-to-10 change; opportunity to revisit before SFI; CFI is not a commitment to ship.
  - Forkcast view: [client priority page](https://forkcast.org/upgrade/hegota/client-priority/?quick=cl).

sections.heading: EIP-8379 Top Up Sync
sections.summary: Top Up Sync DFI'd for Hegotá after limited support; proponents encouraged to experiment with optional engine API endpoints outside the fork.
sections.body:
- Dustin (champion) presented the EIP: adds an engine API endpoint (engine_getSyncStatus) so the CL can query the EL's sync state and drive sync from the right point.
  - Enables resilience (CL can sync EL after incidents like Holesky/Pectra where both layers got stuck simultaneously).
  - Reduces duplicate gossip traffic; ELs can optionally stop listening to certain gossip.
  - Reduces attack surface; enables flexible storage deduplication between CL and EL.
  - Not intended to replace snap sync; complementary for serial top-up after snapshot.
- Łukasz Rozmej (Nethermind) initially expressed concern about losing control over EL sync optimization, but after clarification acknowledged the EIP only adds an informational endpoint and doesn't mandate behavioral changes.
- Enrico Del Fante (Teku) argued that without deciding the end-game vision for CL/EL responsibility separation, adding optional capabilities in both directions doesn't address the core issue; real deduplication requires picking a direction.
- Cayman (Lodestar) voiced support, viewing it as a minor engine API tweak that unlocks optional flexibility.
- ethDreamer (Lighthouse) supported it in principle as an engine API change but wanted more time to assess implementation effort; would have preferred deferral over DFI.
- Marius Van Der Wijden questioned whether it's worth implementing across 5+ clients at this stage.
- Decision: DFI'd for Hegotá, with understanding that teams interested in the functionality can experiment with it outside the fork cadence.

sections.heading: EIP-8383 Reduce CL Block Retention Window
sections.summary: Deferred to next ACDC call; client teams asked to review the EIP before then.
sections.body:
- Kevaundray Wedderburn (champion) noted there have been many conversations about retention windows, but acknowledged clients may not have reviewed the EIP yet.
- Barnabas suggested deferring to the next call.
- Agreement: deferred; client teams have homework to review EIP-8383 before the next ACDC.

sections.heading: EIP-8025 Optional Execution Proofs
sections.summary: Discussion began but deferred to next call due to time; Nethermind raised concerns about shipping non-production-ready features and zkVM pairing governance.
sections.body:
- Ignacio (ethrex / champion) proposed CFI for EIP-8025, emphasizing it defines specs for optional proofs without committing to any specific zkVM pairing or proof system.
  - Key motivation: upstreaming work into a shared repository to de-risk analysis of how zkVMs interact with other protocol changes (e.g., PVD); maintaining separate zkVM and PVD spec branches is increasingly inefficient.
- Łukasz Rozmej (Nethermind) raised two objections despite loving execution proofs generally:
  - Historically, fork-shipped features are production-ready; optional proofs won't be secure enough without gas repricing, sending mixed signals to the community.
  - The current solution involves committee-selected guest program / zkVM pairings, breaking the culture of open client competition.
- Ignacio responded that these concerns are more relevant to mandatory proofs, not EIP-8025's optional proofs, which don't enshrine any proof system.
- Decision deferred to next ACDC call due to time constraints.
